cues.text: In this town, everyone got a superpower
on the day they turned eighteen.
The bell rang once, and you had one.
Nobody knew who handed them out.
And nobody got a good one.
My mother could find any lost sock.
Only socks.
The oldest man could breathe underwater.
For two seconds.
I was born on the same day as my brother.
I wore red. He wore black.
He also kicked the pigs.
He pushed the sheep into the pond, and he laughed.
I pulled them out. He laughed at that too.
One morning, my father took him by the hand.
He said a village over the hills could teach a boy to be kind.
He said, "I will be back soon."
I watched them go until the black shirt was a dot.
I waited at the gate that night.
And the next night.
Then it was winter.
Then it was ten winters.
After a while, I forgot what he looked like.
But every night, my mother set four plates.
So I grew up helping.
I carried my mother's water.
I fixed the baker's roof.
And I had three friends: Bo, Mira, and Tip.
It was actually a pretty good life.
Bo turned eighteen first. The bell rang.
He could jump one block higher than anyone else.
Mira could make any bread warm again, just by touching it.
Tip always knew which way was north.
He told us. Constantly.
Somewhere over the hills, my brother was turning eighteen too.
What would the bell give a boy who kicked pigs?
In the morning the bell rang, and the whole town watched.
For a second, nothing happened.
Then one small daisy came up next to my foot.
That was it. That was my power.
The town laughed for a week.
I hated it.
Bo could jump. Mira had warm hands. Even Tip had north.
I had a flower.
Every evening they showed off at the bell. I went home early.
So I never used it. Not once.
I never noticed that the grass was always greener where I slept.
Then one morning, I woke up to screaming.
The street was full of smoke.
Tip ran past shouting, "North! It came from the north!"
Where was my mother? What was happening?
I got to the door, and my house exploded.
I landed on my back in the road.
Someone was standing in the smoke.
A black shirt.
My brother. Eighteen, and smiling.
He held out his hand to help me up.
I got up by myself.
He said, "I have a kingdom now, over the hills."
"Everyone in it does what I say. I want my brother beside me."
He said it the way he used to talk to the pigs.
I asked where our father was. He only smiled.
I looked behind me.
Every roof was burning. Everyone I knew was running.
And then I saw her. My mother, far down the road, looking at me.
She was still holding one sock.
Something in my chest went hot.
I pushed him as hard as I could.
He did not move an inch.
Then Bo jumped at him, one block higher than anyone.
My brother caught him by the arm.
Bo's jump went out of him like a light.
And my brother jumped. One block higher.
That was when I saw it.
His power was not fire. It was not explosions. It was not strength.
His power was taking powers. A whole village of them.
I was not angry any more. I was scared.
He flicked me with one finger.
I flew over the well, over the bell, and into the mud by the pig pen.
It should have broken everything. I felt nothing.
He walked towards me, slowly. I waited for the end.
Then I saw my hands.
I lifted them. Where they had been, the mud was grass.
With one daisy in it.
"Did I do this?"
The pig beside me had a burned ear. I touched it. The ear grew back.
My power was never a flower. My power was life.
He had a hundred powers, and all of them could only break.
I stood up, and I said, "I know how to beat you."
Like and subscribe for part two.
